catalog_quote: [p. 343, item 3] Имеется подвижное тональное ударение. Акцентные парадигмы не изучены. В ударном слоге различается четыре тональных акцента: H, L, R, F. Примеры: ... Тональные акценты нуждаются в дальнейшем изучении, в словаре они не отмечались. [p. 318] В четырех говорах установлено сосуществование тона и словесного ударения: гигатлинском диалекте чамалинского, дюбекском диалекте табасаранского, чадаколобском диалекте аварского и лучекском диалекте рутульского. Проакцентуированы словари двух первых говоров, во втором их них тоны различаются лишь на ударных гласных. Возможно, что и в некоторых других языках со словесным ударением сохранились тоны. Словесное ударение в дагестанских языках всегда подвижное и неавтоматическое. В большинстве иктусовых языков оно падает на один из первых двух слогов слова.

new_statements.translation: [p. 343] There is mobile tonal stress. Accent paradigms have not been studied. On the stressed syllable four tonal accents are distinguished: H, L, R, F. [...] The tonal accents need further study; they were not marked in the wordlist. [p. 318] In four varieties the coexistence of tone and word stress has been established: the Gigatli dialect of Chamalal, the Dyubek dialect of Tabasaran, the Chadakolob dialect of Avar and the Luchek dialect of Rutul. [...] Word stress in the Dagestanian languages is always mobile and non-automatic. In most of the stress (ictus) languages it falls on one of the first two syllables of the word.

Тональные акценты нуждаются в дальнейшем изучении, в словаре они не отмечались.' (the text has scanned noise '…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Rutul has word stress that is mobile and not phonologically predictable, confined to a window of the first two syllables (Kodzasov 1990:318; Kodzasov 2003:64). In Luchek Rutul the stressed syllable additionally carries one of four tonal accents (H, L, R, F), and accent paradigms are unstudied. The primary grammars, seen only in snippets and via Borise's survey, give the placement tendency inside the window: in nouns stress as a rule falls on the second syllable from the beginning (Ibragimov 1978 §45, Mukhad dialect: 'В именах, как правило, оно падает на второй слог от начала'; Ibragimov 2004:47), in verbs on the first (Alekseev 1994:218: 'Stress may fall on the first or second syllable of a word.. tends to be the second in nouns, but the first in verbs').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned by Kodzasov 1990. Dzhejranishvili 1967 (snippet) speaks of a secondary ('побочное') dynamic stress alongside the musical stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Kodzasov: accent paradigms unstudied (i.e. stress shifts in inflection). Via Borise/Ibragimov: monosyllables shift stress onto vowel-initial suffixes (χud - χudá), pretonic vowel syncope (ubúl - ublís), stress-repelling plural -bɨr vs stress-attracting -ba/-mar/-ar/-abar; Mukhrek dialect retracts to first syllable in some case forms (Ibragimov 1978:147); Ikhrek dialect penultimate (Ibragimov 1978:165); Dzhejranishvili's rival analysis: pitch stress on the penult.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (citation forms in a phonetic wordlist); Kodzasov describes the Luchek village variety only and explicitly says tones were not marked in the wordlist. Ibragimov's placement statement is for the Mukhad dialect. The language is thus described both as a stress language with a two-syllable window (Kodzasov, Alekseev, Ibragimov) and as having tonal/pitch accent (Dzhejranishvili; Kodzasov for Luchek), so the record is partly contradictory across sources.
new_statements.identity_note: Kodzasov's sketch (Kibrik & Kodzasov 1990:342-343) describes the speech of Luchek village (Rutul district, Dagestan; northern/Mukhad dialect area), not the whole language. Ibragimov's second-syllable rule is stated for the Mukhad dialect (basis of the literary language); the Ikhrek dialect is reported as penultimate (Ibragimov 1978:165 via Borise) and Dzhejranishvili's penult pitch-stress analysis is based on Mukhad. Glottolog 5.1 assigns no separate glottocodes to the Rutul dialects (Mukhad, Shinaz, Ikhrek-Myukhrek, Borch-Khnov), so the entry stays under rutu1240.

tone_statements.citation: Ibragimova, Lejla Magomedovna. 2009. Mjuxrekskij dialekt rutul'skogo jazyka [The Myukhrek dialect of Rutul]. Dissertacija kand. filol. nauk (10.02.02), Makhachkala. 133 pp. Ch. I 'Fonetika mjuxrekskogo dialekta', §1.7 'Udarenie'.
tone_statements.quote: Ударение в мюхрекском диалекте, как и в общерутульском, определяется высотою голосового тона и реализуется несколькими восходящими и нисходящими разновидностями. В принципе ударение в рутульском оценивается как тональное. В мюхрекском присутствует элемент длительности, связанный с эмоциональностью (эта особенность присуща сувангильскому диалекту ца-хурского языка). Долгие гласные оцениваются как ударные.
tone_statements.translation: Stress in the Myukhrek dialect, as in common Rutul, is determined by the height of the voice pitch and is realised in several rising and falling varieties. In principle, stress in Rutul is assessed as tonal. In Myukhrek there is an element of length connected with emotionality (a feature also proper to the Suvagil dialect of Tsakhur). Long vowels are assessed as stressed.
tone_statements.locator: Zakljuchenie (conclusion) of the dissertation as reproduced on the dissercat record page, phonetics summary paragraph (corresponds to ch. I §1.7 'Udarenie'); page number not shown
tone_statements.summary: Word stress realised by pitch: several rising and falling accent varieties on the stressed syllable (number not given in the excerpt); stress called 'tonal'; vowel length treated as a correlate (long vowels = stressed), with an emotive length element in Myukhrek; no placement rule in the served text.

tone.quote: In modern Lezghian languages there is either no accent (as in Kryz and most Tsakhur dialects), or it is extremely morphologized ... Independent distinctions in the place of accent may be discovered only in Rutul (in nouns; the positioning of accent in the verb is yet unclear), in the Gelmets dialect of Tsakhur, and, possibly, in the Tabasaran verbal system. ... the MSU expeditions have discovered tonal systems in some Lezghian languages (in the Northern dialect of Tabasaran, in Tsakhur, Kryz and Budukh). ... It is possible that the afore-mentioned non-standard accent systems in Rutul and in the Gelmets dialect of Tsakhur, as well as accent archaisms in Archi, are reflections of the PL tonal system.
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone.summary: Accent statement only: lexically free accent place in Rutul nouns (verbs undetermined); Rutul is not counted among the Lezgian languages with recorded tone systems; authors hypothesise its accent system continues Proto-Lezgian tone. No tone inventory for Rutul.
